Stack the quality scores of several runs into one table

Source: R/compare-runs.R
compare_runs.Rd

One 01_mhc_overview render scores one subset. compare_runs() stacks the per-sample score tables of several renders (different experiments, subsets, or the same QC standard measured over time) into a single long table, so that they can be compared side by side with summarise_runs() and plot_run_trend().

Usage

compare_runs(runs, labels = NULL, order = c("input", "timestamp"))

Arguments

runs

A character vector of score-csv paths and/or results folders, a single score_sample_quality() data frame, or a list of any of these. Names, when given, become the run labels.

labels

Optional character vector of run labels, one per run after folders have been expanded. Overrides every other label source.

order

"input" (default) keeps the runs in the order given; "timestamp" orders them by render_timestamp (oldest first), for a longitudinal view. Runs without a timestamp go last, with a warning.

Value

The stacked score table: one row per (run, sample), with the leading columns Run (a factor in run order), SampleSet, Subset, MHCclass, ThresholdMode, render_timestamp, package_version and source_file, followed by the score columns. Columns are the union over runs: a metric one run lacks is NA there. Labels default to the input names, then SampleSet | Subset from the companion params, then the file name.

Details

runs may mix three kinds of input:

  • a score csv written by 01_mhc_overview (<Subset>_scores.csv, or scores.csv when no Subset was set);

  • a results folder holding one or more such files (e.g. <FolderResults>/<Subset>); every *scores.csv in it becomes a run;

  • a data frame returned by score_sample_quality().

For a csv, the companion <Subset>_01_mhc_overview_input_params.csv that the same render writes next to it is read when present (for results written before v0.27.0, the old <Subset>_05_quality_score_input_params.csv), and its SampleSet, Subset, MHCclass, ThresholdMode, render_timestamp and package_version are attached as columns (NA when absent, and always for data-frame input).

Composite scores are only comparable when the runs were scored the same way, so a warning names the runs when MHCclass or ThresholdMode differs between them: the class selects the threshold table, and "qc_relative" thresholds are calibrated on each run's own QC samples.

See also

summarise_runs(), plot_run_trend(), score_sample_quality()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
runs <- compare_runs(c(jy = "3_results/dda_jy", plasma = "3_results/dda_plasma"))
summarise_runs(runs)
plot_run_trend(runs)
} # }
